key_insight: Coarse attention-based signals mislead hallucination detection because hidden confounders (like token position and object repetition) produce Simpson's paradox; a Bayesian probe that models these confounders and uncertainty yields reliable per-object hallucination probabilities and enables targeted mitigation.
problem_solved: Detecting and reducing object hallucinations in image captions generated by large vision-language models, overcoming unreliable attention-based heuristics.
method: Diagnose why attention-based detection fails by identifying confounders (token position, repetition) and demonstrating Simpson's paradox in coarse analyses.
Introduce HaloProbe: a Bayesian probe that estimates per-object hallucination probability while explicitly modeling confounders and predictive uncertainty.
Use the probe's probabilistic scores for mitigation (e.g., uncertainty-aware decoding or post-hoc correction/calibration) to reduce spurious object mentions.
impact: Provides a principled, uncertainty-aware tool to reliably flag and reduce object hallucinations, improving trustworthiness and safety of vision-language systems in downstream applications.
visual_elements: Simple schematic illustrating Simpson's paradox: aggregated attention trend vs. stratified/by-position trend
Architecture flowchart: image + caption → HaloProbe (Bayesian module) → per-object probability → mitigation
Precision/recall or calibration curves comparing attention-only baseline vs. HaloProbe
Before/after example captions with hallucinated objects highlighted and probability scores shown
paper_title: HaloProbe: Bayesian Detection and Mitigation of Object Hallucinations in Vision-Language Models
paper_authors: Reihaneh Zohrabi, Hosein Hasani, Akshita Gupta, Mahdieh Soleymani Baghshah, Anna Rohrbach
